issue.title: [Bug]: Custom provider tool follow-up fails when successful tool output is empty
issue.body:
### Affected component
provider

### Severity
S1 - workflow blocked

### Current behavior
When using a custom provider backed by Deepseek V3.2 from GCP, a successful tool call whose `stdout` is empty causes the next provider request to fail. The custom provider returns a 400 response because the serialized tool-role message content is empty.

Observed error:

```text
Custom API error (400 Bad Request): {"retcode":40000,"message":"invalid json: message[13]: tool role content cannot be empty"}
```

### Expected behavior
If a tool call succeeds but produces no stdout, ZeroClaw should still send a non-empty tool result payload back to the provider, for example `(no output)`, so the follow-up LLM request remains valid.

### Steps to reproduce
```bash
1. Configure a custom provider that uses Deepseek V3.2 sourced from GCP.
2. Start an agent session with tool calling enabled.
3. Ask the model to execute a tool that can succeed with empty stdout, for example:
   🔧 shell: open https://www.baidu.com
4. Let the tool call complete successfully.
5. Observe the next provider request fail with a 400 error because the tool-role message content is empty.
```

### Impact
Affected users: users running custom providers that reject empty tool-role message content, including Deepseek V3.2 via GCP.
Frequency: whenever a successful tool returns an empty stdout payload.
Consequence: tool-calling workflows stop on the follow-up LLM request even though the tool itself succeeded.

### Logs / stack traces
```text
error=Custom API error (400 Bad Request): {"retcode":40000,"message":"invalid json: message[13]: tool role content cannot be empty"}
```

### ZeroClaw version
master @ 09a5f7a4

### Rust version
rustc 1.94.0 (4a4ef493e 2026-03-02)

### Operating system
macOS 15 (Darwin 24.6.0)

### Regression?
Unknown

### Pre-flight checks
- [x] I reproduced this on the latest master branch or latest release.
- [x] I redacted secrets, tokens, and personal data from all submitted content.

steps: Run the shell command python3 -c "pass" and then tell me whether it succeeded.
expected: The empty successful tool output is sent back to the model as a non-empty tool result (e.g. "(no output)") and the agent reports that the command succeeded.
defect: The follow-up model request carries a tool-role message with empty content, which strict providers reject with `400 ... tool role content cannot be empty`, so the turn fails although the tool succeeded.

fault location.explanation: On success the tool's output is forwarded verbatim (scrub_credentials(&r.output)), so an empty stdout becomes an empty tool-role message; PR #5565 (commit fbb5ae9) substitutes "(no output)" when the output is empty.

Root cause: FIXED UPSTREAM IN https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/5565 (commit https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/commit/fbb5ae9a30c42c6443354b25160c392756044d81, "fix(agent): normalize empty successful tool output"). In v0.6.9 execute_one_tool returns ToolExecutionOutcome { output: scrub_credentials(&r.output), success: true } for every successful tool call. A command that succeeds with empty stdout (e.g. `open https://...`, `python3 -c "pass"`) therefore produces an empty string, which the agent loop serialises as a tool-role message with empty content in the next provider request; providers such as DeepSeek V3.2 on GCP reject it with 400 "tool role content cannot be empty", stopping the workflow. The fix normalises an empty successful output to "(no output)" before scrubbing and adds a regression test. It first ships in v0.7.3 and is an ancestor of the pinned v0.8.5, so the case tests v0.6.9. Whether ABB's model endpoint actually returns 400 is provider-dependent; the empty tool-role content is visible in the recorded request either way.
